Active or completed jobs return 409; invalid passwords return 400. The override is saved only in private queue state so it survives restart, and is excluded from job responses and diagnostics. Catalogue `archivePassword` values are public source metadata, distinct from the user override. The browser masks entry; the native app uses its on-screen keyboard.

### Archive inspection

A release with `archiveContents: "unverified"` uses `format: "Unknown"`, declares `compression` and omits `extractedBytes`. The public UI uses the packaging label and compressed `sizeBytes`. After downloading, the job enters `inspecting`, then `extracting` after validating safe names, regular file/directory types, sizes and the measured free-space requirement. A recognised game layout is not required. Active inspection supports pause/cancel. Jobs expose `inspectedBytes` and `detectedFormat` after inspection (`Unknown` when the layout is not recognised); `extractTotal` uses those bytes without changing the pinned release. Unsafe or damaged archives and insufficient space retain the archive. Resume repeats inspection from that file and does not repeat the network transfer.

## Add-on catalogue (v8, introduced in 1.5.0)

Authenticated `GET /api/v1/addons` returns add-on download options separately from `GET /api/v1/catalog`, whose base-game response is unchanged. Options include `addonId`, `baseGameId`, `baseGameTitle`, `addonType`, `contents`, selected title/content IDs and `requirements` (`titleIds`, `edition`, `minimumVersion`, `notes`). Credentials and provider URLs remain private. Catalogue status reports `addonCount` separately from `gameCount`.

Queue and receive snapshots retain this identity and the selected requirements. A catalogue refresh cannot turn an existing DLC download into a base-game download. Installation receipts identify a completed transfer and each package/content identity; a shared base-game title ID does not imply that its DLC is installed.

## Game updates and Get everything (v8, introduced in PS4 0.1.0)

`GET /api/v1/game-updates` returns PS4 game updates (patches) separately from games and add-ons, shaped like `GET /api/v1/addons` rows: provider URLs removed, `browserAvailable` and `directAvailable` added, rows from disabled sources left out. Each row has `updateId` (equal to its `gameId`), `baseGameId`, `baseGameTitle`, `updateVersion` (`"1.27"`), `requiredFirmware` (the oldest firmware the file runs on, `"9.00"`) and `backport`. A row whose firmware is newer than the console's adds `firmwareIssue: "newer-firmware"` and `consoleFirmware`. Update rows never appear in `/api/v1/catalog`, `/api/v1/sources` counts them as `updateReleaseCount` and `/api/v1/catalog/updates` as `updateCount`, apart from games and add-ons. Older apps ignore the feed's `updates` array.

`GET /api/v1/library` adds `installedVersion` to each installed PS4 game: the higher of the APP_VER in its param.sfo and in an installed `patch.pkg`, or `""` when neither can be read. A game whose catalogue has a newer update this console runs also gets `update: {gameId, version, baseGameId, requiredFirmware}`; the top level adds `updateCount`. The service picks the highest version whose `requiredFirmware` is not newer than the console's (any, when the firmware is unknown), and for the same version the newest firmware build that still runs (a native build over a backport). Nothing is offered when the installed version is unknown.

`GET /api/v1/system` reports `bundleProtocol: 1` when the service has `/api/v1/game-updates` and `/api/v1/bundles`; Orbit Zero offers Get everything and Update only then.

`POST /api/v1/bundles` (paired) adds an ordered list to Downloads, one item at a time: `{"action":"start","storageId":"internal","items":[{"releaseId":"…","delivery":"direct"|"torbox"}],"installInOrder":true,"returnToOrbit":false}`. `delivery` is optional per item; without it the console chooses as a plain Download would. The whole list is checked first: 1–64 distinct items (400), every release in the catalogue (404, "This item isn't in the PS4's catalogue yet. Refresh the catalogue on the PS4, then try again."), every source enabled (409), and room on the drive for all of them after unfinished downloads (409, "Not enough space for everything on this drive."). Only one list runs at a time (409, "Wait for the current Download all to finish."). An item the console can download itself is added at once. An item already in Downloads on that drive isn't added twice: a failed or paused download is retried and a cancelled one that kept its partial file resumed, as Downloads would, and one downloading or downloaded counts as added. One that needs its provider page opens it as a normal Download does, and the next item waits until that page adds its file. If that page is closed or fails, an ordered list stops and the rest are marked `skipped`; an unordered one carries on. `{"action":"cancel","id":"…"}` stops adding; what was added stays. `GET /api/v1/bundles` returns `{id, state: idle|running|page|done|stopped, message, installInOrder, items:[{releaseId, title, kind: game|update|dlc, state: pending|adding|page|added|failed|skipped, jobId, message}]}`. The list itself is kept in memory only.

Every download a list adds has `autoInstall: true`: its packages install once checked. With `installInOrder`, each also has `installAfter`, the previous download's job ID, and waits until that download's packages are installed. Its receipt then shows `chain: "waiting"`, `chainTitle` and the message "Installs after {title}.". If the earlier download failed to install, was cancelled or was left for the user to install, nothing installs automatically: `chain: "blocked"` and "Install {title} first, then select Install.". Clients translate these from `chain` and `chainTitle`. Update downloads carry `updateId`, `updateVersion`, `baseGameId` and `baseGameTitle`, and are titled "{game} · Update {version}".

### Optional support links

Authenticated `GET /api/v1/support` returns `{ "links": [{ "label": "Support with crypto", "url": "https://github.com/saawant12/orbit-store-ps5/issues/131#user-content-support-with-crypto", "qr": ["…"] }] }`. Each QR row contains binary module values; clients add a four-module quiet zone. The service reads only the public project’s `.github/FUNDING.yml`, at most once every six hours when the support screen is opened, with a six-second timeout. A valid cached configuration is retained on failure, falling back to the bundled official links. Funding supports known provider keys and HTTPS custom links in scalar, inline-list or block-list form, bounded to 16 links and 16 KiB. Credentials, local destinations and non-HTTPS custom URLs are rejected. Zero exposes the same shape through authenticated `GET /api/support` and opens only configured destinations through its desktop IPC.

Authenticated `GET /api/v1/announcements` returns `{ "announcements": [{ "id": "new-games-2026-11-03", "title": "…", "message": "…", "translations": { "de": { "title": "…", "message": "…" } } }], "refreshing": false }`: the entries of the public project’s `announcements.json` that show now for this service version, in file order, at most 10 ([format](announcements.md)). The service fetches the file in a background worker at most hourly with a six-second timeout. While `refreshing` is true, the response contains the cached entries and clients should check again shortly. The last valid copy stays in the state folder; a 404 clears it. An unreadable or invalid feed retains that copy, or returns an empty list if none exists. An invalid entry is left out on its own. Each app remembers which announcements it has shown. Zero reads the same file asynchronously and exposes the announcement list through authenticated `GET /api/announcements`.

## Removing history and downloaded files

`POST /history` accepts `{action:"settings",choice:"ask"|"keep"|"delete"}`.
The preference is shared by PS4 clients. The default is `ask`; old remove/forget/
clear-history routes still preserve files. New clients explicitly send the choice.

`{action:"preview",ids:[...]}` returns the preference and each selected download's
original file paths, actual byte sizes, `deleteAllowed` and an explanatory error.
Only completed/cancelled jobs qualify. `{action:"remove",ids:[...],choice:"keep"|
"delete",remember:true|false}` removes history immediately when keeping files, or
returns 202 while file deletion runs. `removingFiles` and `removalError` in the queue
show progress/failure; a failed deletion retains the entry for inspection/retry.
A retained original archive is included alongside extracted output. Files' drive,
symlink, active-operation and mounted-game guards apply. Installed games are never
uninstalled by these actions. Existing Files controls remain available for other
folders and files.

Completed receiver copies use `/installations/files` with `{origin,action:"preview"|
"delete"}`. The origin must refer to an existing completed receipt below homebrew;
paths are taken from that receipt, not the request. Installation or a protected
ShadowMount source blocks deletion.

## Automatic shutdown

`/power` reports availability, enabled policy, selected `jobId`, state, seconds
and any error. Enabling an idle queue does not itself shut down the console. New
successful work arms the policy; paused/failed work, file operations, pending
installation checks, updates, provider verification windows and a busy Zero client block it. A selected download
must also finish; other unfinished work is always allowed to finish safely.
A failed installation cancels the policy. Cancel during the countdown through any
paired UI to keep the console on. Orbit drains workers and saves progress before
requesting console shutdown. No power command is sent from host tests.

Zero reports its own unfinished work throughout the app, not only while the
Console page is open. Keep Zero running until its queue finishes. If a busy Zero
client disconnects, its hold survives service restarts and does not silently expire; reconnect or explicitly
cancel the shutdown policy. Simulated tests do not establish real-console power
behavior.
